newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks lose 3.42 pct after Wall Street fall.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks lose 3.42 pct after Wall Street fall.

text.p: Thai stocks, hit by heavy declines in major overseas markets and on weak Thai economic indicators, retreated a hefty 3.42 percent on Thursday, brokers said.
The SET index finished 28.44 points lower at 803.13, a 51-month low, on thin 2.2 billion baht turnover. The indicator last closed lower at 801.90 on September 11, 1992.
The SET-50 blue chip index ended 2.19 points down at 59.09.
"Investors also sold out on concern of Thai economic conditions. Declines on Wall Street and in Hong Kong also hurt the market," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico.
"The December inflation figure did not show any improvement while investors, especially foreigners, are concerned about high current account deficit and falling exports," Thanawat said.
The commerce ministry said the consumer price index rose 4.8 percent year-on-year in December, unchanged from November.
It said the overall 1996 inflation rose to 5.9 percent from 5.8 in 1995.
Brokers expected sustained selling pressure until the current account deficit and exports showed improving trends.
Brokers said sellers unloaded finance, bank and property issues after they bought them late last month.
The finance sector led the decline, losing 8.16 percent, the property counter dipped 4.33 percent, and banks slipped 3.23 percent.
Bangkok Bank topped the active list, shedding five baht to 186, National Finance dropped four to 44, TelecomAsia retreated 4.50 to 49, and Siam Cement declined 20 to 788.
